newsitem.title: ITALY: Versace had been planning market listing for group.
newsitem.headline: Versace had been planning market listing for group.

text.p: The shock murder of Italian fashion design guru Gianni Versace on Tuesday seems certain to derail any immediate plans for the Versace family to float its shares on the world's major stock markets.

Versace, 50, who was shot dead at his Miami mansion, was believed to be planning with his brother Santo and sister Donatella for a listing on the Milan stock market by June 1998. The family-controlled group never officially confirmed the plans.
Gianni was the design genius behind the group and analysts said his death would leave a gaping hole at the creative heart of the company which would be difficult to fill.

"A lot of the value in Versace is tied up in Gianni himself -- not exactly a one-man show but he was very much the front man," said Paul Gordon, luxury goods analyst at Italian broking house IMI Sigeco.

Santo said in an newspaper interview in March that group plans for a flotation for the end of 1997 had to be delayed as the group wanted to complete its restructuring. He said a Milan listing had been put off until in June 1988, to be followed by a possible listing on Wall Street.

Versace and a handful of other designers such as Giorgio Armani had been believed to be thinking of a listing after the stock market success of newly-floated Italian luxury goods groups such as Gucci and Bulgari.

The Milan-based Gianni Versace SpA group is very much a family empire. Santo is chairman and managing director while Donatella is deputy chairman, a designer herself who looks after the Versus line of women and menswear, perfumes and accessories.
The Versace group saw sales rise 23.5 percent in 1996 to 845 billion lire ($485 million), with 80 percent sold abroad, and Versace had seen a further 20 percent rise in sales in 1997.
Group pretax profit for 1996 rose 13.6 percent to 175 billion lire.
Worldwide, Gianni Versace boutiques number 138 with some 345 points of sale plus another 2,600 outlets selling Versace brands Istante, Versus and Versace jeans. ($1=1,750 lire)
